title: Pilgrimage: Kushinagar
hook: the place of the passing, with a great reclining Buddha

segments.voice: Yesterday's pilgrimage stop was Sarnath, the deer park, four truths and four tasks. Your line was where he taught. What did you try to understand before fixing it? Day one thousand three hundred ninety-five.

The statue is long, golden, and lying down. Inside a white temple in a small town in northern India, the Buddha rests on his right side, head propped on his hand, eyes almost closed, feet neatly together. Pilgrims walk slowly around him. Some lay a length of saffron cloth over the body, the way you might tuck a blanket around someone you love. A few people cry. Others sit by the wall and chant. Visitors sometimes take it for a statue of the Buddha napping. It is not. It shows the last hours of his life. This is Kushinagar, the fourth place the Buddha himself named as worth a pilgrim's visit: where he passed away.
screen: `A GOLDEN BUDDHA, LYING DOWN.` → `NOT SLEEPING.` → `THE LAST HOURS.`

segments.voice: The Great Discourse on the Final Passing tells it slowly. First, the posture. Old and ill, the Buddha asks Ananda to set out a couch between twin sal trees, head to the north. He lies down on his right side, one foot on the other, mindful and clear. The text calls it the lion's posture. The trees, it says, burst into bloom out of season and drop their flowers on him. Second, the grief. Ananda goes off alone and weeps. The Buddha sends for him and reminds him gently that he has always taught it: everything dear to us is one day parted from us. Then he praises Ananda's years of kindness in front of everyone. Third, a latecomer. A wanderer named Subhadda arrives with a question, and Ananda tries to turn him away. Do not trouble the teacher, he says. He is weary. The Buddha overhears and lets him in, and teaches him. Even at the end, the door stays open. Fourth, the last words. He asks the monks, again and again, whether anyone has a doubt left. No one speaks. And then, in Rhys Davids's old translation: "Decay is inherent in all component things! Work out your salvation with diligence!" Buddhists call what followed the parinibbana, the final passing. Pilgrims come to Kushinagar not only to mourn. They come to sit near the place where the teacher, dying, kept teaching.
screen: `ON HIS RIGHT SIDE, LIKE A LION.` · `ANANDA WEEPS.` · `THE DOOR STAYS OPEN.` · then, large: `WORK OUT YOUR SALVATION WITH DILIGENCE.`

segments.voice: Here is a gentle practice, if your body and your space allow it. Lie down on your right side for a minute, on a bed, a couch or a rug, one foot resting on the other, your head on your hand or a pillow. If you can't lie down, lean a little to the right in your chair. Breathe slowly. Let it be calm, not sad. Remember the trees dropping flowers, and the teacher who used his last strength to answer one more question. When you're ready, sit up slowly. The bell holds the time.
Pilgrimage. Walking to remember. Its fourth great stop is Kushinagar, where the Buddha passed away between the sal trees. Today's word.
Your line: where he passed. Today, let one person in who you might have turned away: a late question, a call, a knock. Day one thousand three hundred ninety-five.

howItsDone: Pilgrims visit Kushinagar in India, walk around the reclining Buddha in the Mahaparinirvana temple, offer robes and flowers, and visit the stupa honored as the place of the cremation.

fork.setup: you're Ananda. your teacher is dying and tired. a stranger arrives at the last hour asking to see him with a question. what do you do?
options: turn him away so the teacher can rest.
fork.reveal: Ananda turned him away, kindly. but the Buddha overheard, called Subhadda in, and taught him. even at the end, the door stayed open.

original.note: Pali parinibbana: the final passing of the Buddha.

trapdoor: what you thought: the reclining Buddha is resting.
what it means: it shows the Buddha's last hours at Kushinagar, lying calm on his right side.
what a scholar hears: the lion's posture between twin sal trees, Subhadda let in at the last hour, and the final words on diligence.

notes: Quotation from Rhys Davids, Buddhist Suttas (Sacred Books of the East XI, 1881), Book of the Great Decease VI.10. Confirm exact wording and punctuation.

DN 16 ch. 5 paraphrased: couch between twin sal trees with head to the north, lion's posture on the right side, sal trees blooming out of season, Ananda weeping and being comforted and praised, Subhadda admitted. Confirm.
'He asks the monks, again and again' paraphrases the threefold asking; the number was left out per the claims rule.
Hook: 'the fourth place the Buddha himself named' refers to the four places in DN 16 ch. 5; confirm acceptable under the claims rule.
Hook description of the Mahaparinirvana temple's reclining image (golden, saffron cloth offerings) is descriptive; confirm.
howItsDone mentions the cremation stupa (Ramabhar); confirm.
